title: `dev` is two concurrent shell pipelines with no anvil-ownership or genesis-freshness check: DeployMocks silently broadcasts a full rehearsal onto a pre-existing chain
description:
`"dev": "npm run clean:local && npm run start:anvil & sleep 3 && LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU=true npm run deploy:local && ..."` — `&` binds looser than `&&`, so this is TWO pipelines. Pipeline A (`clean:local && start:anvil`) is backgrounded and its exit status is DISCARDED. Pipeline B is gated on a bare `sleep 3` with no port probe, no `cast block-number` poll, and no check that the anvil answering on 8545 is the one pipeline A started. `DeployMocks.s.sol` contains exactly one reference to the chain it is running on — `console.log("Chain ID:", block.chainid)` at :392 — and no assertion of any kind.

Reproduced empirically. With a pre-existing anvil already listening on 8545 (the state Ctrl-C out of `npm run serve` always leaves behind, because `serve` blocks forever and only the foreground pipeline dies), `npm run dev` produced: pipeline A `Error: Address already in use (os error 98)` (swallowed, exit status discarded); `[PIPELINE_B] proceeded, dollar-question=0`; port 8545 still held by the ORIGINAL anvil (pid 57286) at block 11, deployer nonce 1. `deploy:local` then simulated cleanly — including `end-state phUSD ACL asserted` and the Phase 7.6 dispatcher-swap rehearsal — and BROADCAST 265 transactions onto that non-genesis chain, driving the deployer nonce 1 -> 267. Every one of DeployMocks' own post-conditions passed, and `progress.31337.json` was rewritten as if the chain were fresh.

CRITICAL DISTINCTION FROM LEDGER ENTRY L-02 (ce524709d965, open), which proposes `require(block.chainid == 31337)`: the stale chain IS chainId 31337. Verified by `cast chain-id --rpc-url http://localhost:8545` -> 31337 on the pre-existing anvil. L-02's proposed fix would PASS and catch nothing here. This is a distinct root cause — a missing genesis-freshness assertion, not a missing network assertion.

The precondition is not exotic: it is produced by the normal end of a successful run. Confirmed at teardown of the clean full run — after `serve` was killed, `npm run dev` returned EXIT 0 and pipeline A's anvil was still listening on 8545 answering `eth_chainId` -> `0x7a69`, and had to be killed by PID. Every ordinary `dev` session therefore ends by arming the next one.
impact: `dev` is not merely a dev-stack boot; it is the local rehearsal of the mainnet PhlimboV2->V3 cutover, the dispatcher swap and the terminal privilege sweep (`DeployMocks.s.sol:95` states the local and mainnet paths are deliberately 'the same code operating through the same interface'), and its green output is read as evidence that those mainnet procedures are sound. Under the stale-anvil mode every assertion still passes while the run is layered on top of an arbitrary prior deployment — addresses, nonces, phUSD ACL state and dispatcher indices are all inherited rather than established. A rehearsal that silently certifies itself on the wrong chain state is worse than one that fails, because the failure is invisible and the artefact it emits (`progress.31337.json`) is indistinguishable from a good run. Ceiling is Medium, not High: this is local-only, never touches mainnet funds, and requires an operator-created precondition.
evidence: side-effects.json -> raceReproduction. Commands: `anvil --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8545 --chain-id 31337 --block-time 2` (pre-existing), then `npm run dev`; `cast chain-id/block-number/nonce --rpc-url http://localhost:8545`; scratchpad logs stale-anvil.log, race.log, deploy-onto-stale.log.
recommendation: Add a genesis-freshness gate to `DeployMocks.run()` alongside the chain-id gate, before `vm.startBroadcast`: `require(block.chainid == 31337, "DeployMocks: local only"); require(vm.getNonce(deployer) == 0, "DeployMocks: chain is not fresh - a prior deployment is already on 8545; kill it and re-run");`. Independently, make the shell honest: replace `& sleep 3` with a foreground readiness loop that both (a) starts anvil and captures its PID, and (b) polls `cast block-number` until it answers, then verifies the responding node is the PID just started; and add a `trap` that kills the background anvil on exit so Ctrl-C out of `serve` cannot leave the stale-chain precondition behind. Note explicitly in the L-02 remediation that the chain-id guard alone does NOT close this.

title: `dev` hardcodes `LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU=true`, making the dormant (day-one mainnet) leg unreachable through the only entry point developers run — partially reverting the story-079 fix for ledger L-03
description:
Ledger entry L-03 (12bcca3b617c, fix-pending) was fixed correctly at the contract-script layer: `DeployMocks.s.sol:398` now reads `armKenduPromo = vm.envOr("LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU", true)` and a full dormant leg exists (:400, :1631-1639, :2044-2061, :2193-2199). That is exactly what story 079 mandated, armed-by-default included. This delta then added `LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU=true` to the `dev` key itself.

A command-prefix assignment overrides the inherited environment, so the toggle is now inert from outside. Verified: `LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU=false bash -c 'LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU=true sh -c "echo \$LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU"'` -> `true` (control without the prefix -> `false`). A developer following the instruction the script itself prints cannot make it take effect.

The script contradicts the entry point in three places. `DeployMocks.s.sol:210` NatSpec: "Set LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU=false to boot the DORMANT chain instead — the state mainnet actually ships on day one, and the one state this script could previously never produce." `:1634` prints at the end of EVERY `dev` run: "Set LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU=false to boot the DORMANT (day-one mainnet) chain" (captured verbatim in the live run log). And `:1984`: "Do not read the armed leg's behaviour as a prediction of mainnet's." `dev` pins the rehearsal to precisely the leg its author says must not be read as a prediction, and the remedy the script advertises does not work.

This is NOT an incomplete fix of L-03 as filed — the fix landed complete. It is a correct fix partially reverted one layer up, by one of the nine untagged commits in this delta.
impact: The day-one mainnet configuration (`promoToken == address(0)`, `promoRewardBalance == 0`, phUSD/Kendu streams whitelisted-but-unregistered) is unreachable through `npm run dev` without editing package.json. Story 076 specifies mainnet ships with 'No `startPromotion` call anywhere'; the shape the UI must actually render gracefully on day one is therefore never exercised by the entry point anyone runs, while the divergent armed shape is. Local-only, so no funds are at risk — but it degrades the evidentiary value of the rehearsal and it silently undoes work a human triaged as fix-pending, which is exactly the class the ledger's INCOMPLETE-FIX rule exists to catch. Propose the L-03 ledger entry be held at fix-pending pending this revert, NOT flipped to fixed.
evidence: package.json:16; DeployMocks.s.sol:210-213, :398-400, :1631-1639, :1984; live `dev` run log (sim-log.txt) line 'LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU (Kendu promo armed on PhlimboV3): true' and 'Set LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU=false to boot the DORMANT (day-one mainnet) chain'; shell-override reproduction above. Status proposal only — no ledger status flipped.
recommendation: Delete `LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU=true` from the `dev` key and let `vm.envOr`'s default supply the armed leg (identical behaviour, toggle restored). If an explicit armed default is wanted at the npm layer, add a second key (`dev:dormant` with `LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU=false`) rather than pinning the only one. Add a rehearsal obligation that BOTH legs are booted before a mainnet cutover, since only the dormant leg matches day one.

title: Gating `_seedNudgeStream` on `LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU` silently disables a load-bearing fee-on-transfer probe on the dormant leg, contrary to story 079's explicit instruction
description:
This delta moved `nudgeStreamer.registerStream(phUSD)`, `registerStream(mockKendu)` and both `_seedNudgeStream` calls inside `if (armKenduPromo) { ... } else { ... }` (`git diff 1d8a3a7 f929b5b -- script/DeployMocks.s.sol`). Story 079 states verbatim: "**Do NOT gate the Kendu nudge stream.** `_seedNudgeStream` ... stays unconditional." The same story's closing checklist requires "Confirm no mainnet script, no `src/` contract and no **`package.json` key** was modified" — this delta modified a package.json key (see the L-03-revert finding). Both instructions were violated, by commits carrying no `[story-NNN]` tag at all.

The consequence is concrete rather than cosmetic. `_seedNudgeStream` is self-documented at :2071-2080 as doubling as the fee-on-transfer probe, terminating in `require(received == amount, "nudge seed token is fee-on-transfer: streamer received < sent")` — described in-source as "load-bearing, not decorative". Under the gating, that assertion executes on the armed leg only. The dormant leg — the one that matches day-one mainnet — runs no seeding and therefore no probe.
impact: A safety assertion whose own source comment calls it load-bearing is silently skipped on exactly the configuration that mirrors production. Combined with the `dev` key pinning the armed leg, the current net effect is that the probe always runs today — so there is no live consequence — but the code is now one env-var away from a rehearsal that quietly omits its own guard, and the gating landed without the story authorisation that would have caught it. Low: local-only, no current loss of coverage, but a real Law-2 deviation with a demonstrable safety consequence.
evidence: DeployMocks.s.sol:2044-2061 (gating block), :2069-2096 (`_seedNudgeStream` incl. the load-bearing require at :2096); `git diff 1d8a3a7 f929b5b -- script/DeployMocks.s.sol`; story 079 text at ~/code/product-owner/stories/phStaging2.
recommendation: Either restore the seeding/probe as unconditional per story 079 (registering and seeding the phUSD/Kendu streams costs nothing on the dormant leg beyond two extra streams the UI is supposed to render gracefully anyway), or — if the dormant leg must genuinely leave them unregistered to mirror mainnet — hoist the fee-on-transfer probe out of `_seedNudgeStream` into an unconditional check that runs on both legs, and amend story 079 (or file a superseding story) rather than silently contradicting it.

title: `clean:local` deletes git-TRACKED files and re-runs under a live anvil, wiping scratch state from under the node it is about to broadcast to
description:
`"clean:local": "rm -rf broadcast/*/31337 server/deployments/progress.31337.json server/deployments/local.json && rm -rf ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/*"`.

Two separate problems, both verified.

(1) It deletes TRACKED files. `server/deployments/progress.31337.json` is tracked at HEAD (`git ls-tree f929b5b -- server/deployments/`), and `server/deployments/local.json` was tracked at the diff base 1d8a3a7. Running `clean:local` therefore dirties the working tree with deletions of committed files — observed as `D server/deployments/progress.31337.json` in `git status` after every `dev`. `rm -rf ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/*` additionally reaches OUTSIDE the repository into the developer's home directory, deleting anvil scratch state belonging to any other project.

(2) `deploy:local` re-runs `clean:local` a SECOND time, and by then anvil is already up (pipeline A started it during the `sleep 3`). That second invocation deletes `~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/*` out from under a RUNNING anvil, and deletes `broadcast/*/31337` immediately before the forge run that is about to write it. Neither is currently fatal (anvil holds its state in memory; forge recreates the broadcast dir), so this is latent rather than live — but it is unsynchronised destruction of state belonging to a concurrently-running process, and the ordering that makes it benign is not enforced anywhere.

PRIOR-ENTRY DISCLOSURE. Ledger entry L-02 `ec29eacd9501` on this same entryPoint is WONT-FIX and also concerns `clean:local` — but its subject is different: it records that clean:local deletes the JSON deployment artifacts while leaving the generated TypeScript address files behind (a staleness asymmetry). Neither of the two problems filed here — deletion of git-TRACKED files, and the second invocation running concurrently with a live anvil — is covered by that entry or by the reasoning that closed it. Filed as a distinct root cause, not a re-raise; the owner's wont-fix on the staleness asymmetry is not disturbed.

(3) A third, related artefact of the same design: `server/deployments/addresses.ts` and `server/deployments/local-addresses.ts` are also tracked, are NOT in clean:local's delete list, and are rewritten by `generate:ts-anvil` on every run with a change consisting solely of the generation timestamp (`git diff` after the live run: `-// Generated interface from local.json on 2026-08-10T21:51:16.749Z` / `+// ... 2026-09-07T09:43:08.585Z`, one line each). So every `dev` run guarantees two tracked-file modifications with zero semantic content, on top of the tracked deletions.
impact: Working-tree noise that masks real changes in `git status`/`git diff` for anyone reviewing a `dev` run, deletion of another project's anvil scratch state, and a latent race against the live node. Local-only, recoverable with `git checkout`. Low.
evidence: package.json:8-9; `git ls-tree f929b5b -- server/deployments/` and `git ls-tree 1d8a3a7 -- server/deployments/`; `git status` after a `dev` run showing the tracked deletion.
recommendation: Untrack the generated artefacts (`git rm --cached server/deployments/progress.31337.json server/deployments/local.json` and add both to `.gitignore`) so `clean:local` only ever removes build output — or, if they are wanted as committed fixtures, drop them from the `rm` list and let the deploy overwrite them. Narrow the anvil scratch wipe to a project-scoped path rather than `~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/*`. Remove the leading `npm run clean:local` from `deploy:local` so the wipe happens exactly once, before anvil starts, rather than concurrently with it.

title: `server/index.js` reports a healthy, fully-deployed protocol from a stale tracked progress file with no chain running anywhere
description:
With no anvil running at all and `local.json` absent, `npm run serve` was started standalone and probed:
  - `GET /health` -> HTTP 200, `{"status":"ok", ..., "extractedAddressesLoaded": false}`
  - `GET /contracts` -> HTTP 404
  - startup banner -> `Deployment Status: completed` / `Contracts Deployed: 72`

The banner and `deploymentStatus` are read from `server/deployments/progress.31337.json` (`server/index.js:19-23`), a file that is committed to the repository. Nothing in `/health` (`:88-100`) makes an RPC call, so 'ok' is a statement about the process being alive, not about the protocol being deployed. Story 003's acceptance criterion "GET /health returns success response" is therefore satisfied vacuously and cannot distinguish a working stack from an empty one.

This compounds the stale-anvil race: after a Ctrl-C the server can be restarted against a leftover chain and a committed progress file and report `completed / 72 contracts` for a deployment that does not exist.

RELATED, DISTINCT: ledger L-01 `1e8cc0dc58ba` (open, entryPoint `dev`) records that `progress.31337.json` is WRITTEN with a hard-coded `deploymentStatus: "completed"`. That is the producer-side defect. This finding is the consumer-side one: `/health` and the startup banner READ that file (and, for /health, read nothing at all about the chain) and present it as current liveness. The two fixes are independent — correcting the writer would not stop /health returning 200 with no chain running — but they should be resolved together, and dedup should keep them separate.
impact: The one endpoint an operator or CI job would use to answer 'is the local stack up?' returns success in every state, including total absence of a chain, while the banner actively asserts a completed 72-contract deployment. Local dev only, so no funds or mainnet state are at risk — but the failure mode is silent over-claiming, which is what makes it worth reporting rather than the missing `local.json` on its own.
evidence: `node server/index.js` with port 8545 free and `server/deployments/local.json` absent; `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' localhost:3001/health` -> 200, `/contracts` -> 404; captured banner text. server/index.js:19-23, :88-100, :193-194.
recommendation: Make `/health` actually probe liveness: attempt an `eth_chainId` (or `eth_blockNumber`) against `http://localhost:8545`, plus a code-size check on one deployed address from `local.json`, and return a non-200 (or `status: "degraded"` with an explicit `chainReachable:false`/`addressesLoaded:false`) when either fails. Derive the startup banner from live chain reads rather than from the committed progress file, or label it explicitly as 'last recorded run' so it is not read as current state.

title: `server/deployments/local.json` was removed from git tracking, so `generate:ts-anvil` and `serve` now fail when run standalone
description:
`server/deployments/local.json` was tracked at the diff base (`git ls-tree 1d8a3a7 -- server/deployments/local.json` -> present) and is neither tracked nor present at HEAD (`git ls-tree f929b5b` -> empty; file absent on disk after a clean checkout). It is now produced only by `extract:addresses`, step 4 of the `dev` chain.

Consequence, verified on a clean checkout: `npm run generate:ts-anvil` standalone exits 1 via `generate-ts-addresses.js:101-104` (`if (!fs.existsSync(inputPath)) { ... process.exit(1) }`); `npm run serve` standalone starts but `/contracts` returns 404 (`server/index.js:36-40`). Both keys used to work from a fresh clone. Only the full `dev` chain regenerates the file, and only after a ~15-minute deploy leg.
impact: Two package.json entry points that were previously independently runnable are now hard-coupled to a full local deployment. A developer regenerating TypeScript address bindings, or bringing up only the API against a chain that is already deployed, hits an exit-1 or a 404 with no message explaining that the missing artefact is produced by a different key. Local dev only. Low.
evidence: `git ls-tree 1d8a3a7 -- server/deployments/local.json` vs `git ls-tree f929b5b -- server/deployments/local.json`; `npm run generate:ts-anvil` -> EXIT=1; `npm run serve` + `curl localhost:3001/contracts` -> 404.
recommendation: Either re-track a representative `local.json` (it is generated output, so prefer not to) or, better, make both consumers fail with an actionable message: in `generate-ts-addresses.js:101-104` and `server/index.js:36-40`, name the producing command explicitly — e.g. `local.json not found. Run: npm run extract:addresses (after npm run deploy:local)`. Document the dependency order in the `//local-deploy` comment alongside the existing story-003 reference.

title: `wagmi generate` silently drops the `stableStakerAbi` export and `update:hooks` publishes the result to npm without any failure signal
description:
`wagmi.config.ts:75` requests `'StableStaker.sol/StableStaker.json'`. Story 080's retype landed `import {StableStakerV1} from "stable-staker/versions/v1/StableStakerV1.sol"` in `DeployMocks.s.sol:84`, and `lib/stable-staker/src/StableStaker.sol` no longer exists, so a clean build emits `out/StableStakerV1.sol/StableStakerV1.json` and never `out/StableStaker.sol/StableStaker.json`.

This was initially masked on this machine by a STALE artifact: `out/StableStaker.sol/StableStaker.json` was present but dated 2026-06-12, three months older than the fresh artifacts at 2026-09-07 11:14:53, with metadata still recording the now-deleted source path. Removing that stale artifact and running the generator for real proved the drop: `npx wagmi generate` exited 0, printed all green checkmarks INCLUDING "✔ Resolving contracts", and silently deleted 710 lines from `hooks/generated.ts` — the entire `stableStakerAbi` export, 0 occurrences remaining. No warning, no non-zero exit, nothing an operator or CI gate would catch.

The amplifier is the publish chain: `update:hooks` runs the generator, patches the package version and runs `npm publish`. A clean-checkout CI machine (which by construction has no stale `out/`) therefore publishes a hooks package missing `stableStakerAbi` and reports success.

Second-order nuance worth recording: on a developer machine with the stale artifact, the emitted ABI happens to be signature-identical to StableStakerV1 (63 entries vs 63, zero differences), so the output is correct only by coincidence — which is precisely why the drift went unnoticed.
impact: Downstream consumers of the published hooks package lose the StableStaker bindings entirely, with no build-time or publish-time error — a silent drop is materially worse than a loud failure, because there is no point at which anyone is told. The blast radius is a published npm artifact, not local dev, which is what lifts this above the other `dev`-cluster items. No on-chain funds are at risk.
evidence: wagmi.config.ts:75; DeployMocks.s.sol:84; `ls -l out/StableStaker.sol/StableStaker.json` (mtime 2026-06-12) vs fresh artifacts; after moving the stale artifact aside, `npx wagmi generate` -> exit 0, all checkmarks green, `git diff --stat hooks/generated.ts` -> 710 deletions, `grep -c stableStakerAbi hooks/generated.ts` -> 0.
recommendation: Point the artifact at the type actually deployed: `'StableStakerV1.sol/StableStakerV1.json'` (and export it as `stableStakerV1Abi`, or alias it to keep the consumer-facing name stable). Independently, close the silent-drop class: wagmi's foundry plugin resolves the `artifacts` globs leniently, so add an explicit post-generate assertion to `update:hooks` — fail the script if any expected export name is absent from `hooks/generated.ts` — so a missing artifact can never reach `npm publish`. Delete stale `out/` entries in CI (`forge clean` before `wagmi generate`) so local runs and CI agree.

title: The promotion-ready cutover suite was reduced to `:snapshot` alone, orphaning four operator instructions and removing the only remediation for a fix-pending Medium — with the archived code made uncompilable by design
description:
At the diff base, `promotion-ready:snapshot`, `:dry`, `:broadcast`, `:resume` and `:verify` all existed. At HEAD only `:snapshot` survives (package.json:45). Four doc comments survive alongside it and still instruct operators to run the deleted keys — most explicitly `//order-of-execution:human-readable` at :46: "promotion-ready:snapshot then promotion-ready:dry then promotion-ready:broadcast. ... If the cutover fails, consult Claude on how to resume."

The underlying scripts were moved under `script/archives/`, which `foundry.toml:32` excludes via `skip = ["script/archives/**"]`. They cannot be run even by explicit path: `forge script script/archives/VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol:VerifyPromotionReady --rpc-url $RPC_MAINNET` -> `Error: Could not find target contract`, EXIT=1.

Two aggravating facts. First, `promotion-ready:verify` was created by story 075 specifically to remediate fix-pending Medium `2c53e944caee...` ("A broadcast run performs ZERO on-chain verification of its own outcome"); deleting it removes the accepted fix for a finding a human marked fix-pending, and no story authorises the removal — the purge of ~246 package.json keys has no story anywhere in the tree. Second, the cutover has ALREADY broadcast to mainnet: commit 4e5cca1 landed live addresses and `broadcast/DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol/1/run-latest.json` is tracked. So `:verify` and `:resume` are not hypothetical future tooling — they are the post-hoc verification and recovery path for a migration that is live.

The wider stranding is quantified: 246 keys were deleted in this delta, and 81 live (open or fix-pending) ledger findings had their `entryPoint` deleted by it — including 23 open + 2 fix-pending on `promotion-ready:broadcast`, 3 on `:verify`, 4 on `:resume`, 1 on `:dry`, plus the whole ys-swap and migration-saga families. Their code survives under `script/archives/` but is uncompilable, so neither PoC replay nor `/recheck` has any path to re-prove or retire them.
impact: An operator following the surviving in-repo runbook is told to run three commands, two of which no longer exist and cannot be reinstated by path. The verification step for a migration already executed on mainnet is gone, reopening the exposure story 075 closed. And 81 live findings are frozen in an unresolvable state — not fixed, not abandoned, simply unreachable by the verification tooling. No direct on-chain loss, which caps this at Medium, but it degrades the project's ability to detect or recover from a bad mainnet cutover.
evidence: `git show 1d8a3a7:package.json` vs HEAD (key diff, 246 deletions); package.json:45-46 and the surviving `//promotion-ready`, `//migration-saga`, `//phlimbo-v1-to-v2` comments; foundry.toml:26-32; `forge script script/archives/VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol:VerifyPromotionReady` -> `Could not find target contract`, EXIT=1; `git ls-files broadcast/DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol/1/run-latest.json`; ledger entryPoint tally against reports/phoenix-phase-2-staging/ledger.json.
recommendation: Restore at minimum `promotion-ready:verify` and `promotion-ready:resume` (keys and compilable scripts) — the cutover they cover is already live on mainnet and `:verify` is the accepted fix for fix-pending `2c53e944caee`. For the rest, decide deliberately rather than by sweep: either keep the entry point and its script compiling, or delete the key AND its orphaned doc comment together, and retire the corresponding ledger findings explicitly (`/ledger ... abandon`) rather than leaving them stranded. If `script/archives/**` must stay in `skip`, add a CI check that every path referenced by a surviving package.json key or shell script resolves to a compilable target.

title: `verify-stable-staker.sh` invokes two scripts that were moved to `script/archives/`, and the foundry.toml comment justifying the exclusion is falsified by that very reference
description:
`verify-stable-staker.sh:56` runs `script/interactions/StakeStableStaker.s.sol:StakeStableStaker` and `:67` runs `script/interactions/ClaimWithdrawStableStaker.s.sol:ClaimWithdrawStableStaker`. Both paths are absent at HEAD; both files now live under `script/archives/interactions/`. Running the exact command from the script yields `Error: No such file or directory (os error 2)`, EXIT=1 — the script is dead end-to-end.

`foundry.toml:26-32` justifies `skip = ["script/archives/**"]` with the claim "Nothing outside the directory imports them." That claim is directly falsified by `verify-stable-staker.sh`, which invokes two of them. Per the standing principle that in-source documentation carries no suppression authority, a justification comment that is demonstrably false is itself worth flagging: it is the sentence a future reviewer would rely on to conclude the sweep was safe.
impact: The stable-staker local verification harness — the stake -> warp -> claim/withdraw round trip that proves the StableStaker wiring `dev` just deployed actually works — cannot be run at all. `dev` deploys and wires StableStaker across three pools (observed in the live run: DOLA/USDC/USDe, rates set, 10% set-aside buffer) but nothing exercises it afterwards. Local-only. Low.
evidence: verify-stable-staker.sh:56,:67; `ls script/interactions/` (both absent) vs `ls script/archives/interactions/` (both present); direct invocation -> `Error: No such file or directory (os error 2)`, EXIT=1; foundry.toml:26-32.
recommendation: Repoint the two invocations at `script/archives/interactions/...` and narrow the `skip` glob so those two files still compile (e.g. `skip = ["script/archives/**"]` -> an explicit list, or `git mv` the two interaction scripts back out of `archives/` as story 080 did for its own two files). Correct the foundry.toml comment: it is not true that nothing outside the directory references the archives, and the next sweep will be reasoned about from that sentence.

title: Top-level OpenZeppelin canonicalization to v5.6.1 changes ReentrancyGuard's storage layout relative to four contracts' own pins, creating a tested-bytecode / deployed-bytecode divergence
description:
This delta canonicalizes every nested OpenZeppelin path onto one top-level v5.6.1 checkout, overriding six submodules that pin their own versions. HEAD builds clean under the substitution (`forge build` -> EXIT 0), and roughly 96 reachable-file comparisons across the drifting submodules were made:
  - `Ownable.sol` — byte-identical in all six.
  - `SafeERC20.sol` — rewritten in 5.5.0 but behaviour-preserving, and the `SafeERC20FailedOperation(address)` error selector is unchanged.
  - `ERC4626.sol` — the implementation is not reachable; only `interfaces/IERC4626.sol` is imported.
  - `EnumerableSet.sol` — core byte-identical; 5.x additions (`Bytes4Set`, `Arrays.replace`, `Math.clz`) are purely additive.

ONE genuine divergence. OZ 5.5.0 moved `ReentrancyGuard`'s `uint256 private _status` out of slot 1 into an ERC-7201 namespaced slot (`REENTRANCY_GUARD_STORAGE`). Four in-scope contracts inherit it while pinning a pre-5.5.0 OZ: `StableYieldAccumulator` (pins 5.1.0; live on mainnet at 0x0cD353bfda674D04823B2826ffafB83B560D21B6) and the three `AYieldStrategy` descendants `YieldStrategyDola`, `YieldStrategyUSDe`, `YieldStrategyUSDC` (vault pins 5.4.0). Under the top-level pin, every storage slot after the old slot 1 shifts by one in the bytecode this repository builds and tests.

Deliberately NOT inflated. Nothing here is upgradeable, no proxy is involved, and no first-party code reads a raw storage slot on these contracts (checked for `sload`/`vm.load`/assembly slot access against them). The runtime semantics of the guard are identical. What this is, precisely, is a reproducibility gap: the bytecode `dev` deploys and the test suite exercises is not the bytecode that was deployed to mainnet from the pinned sources.

Compounding: there is NO story for this change. The full 81-file story tree was enumerated; `5.6.1` appears nowhere, no story mentions an OZ pin, version or remapping change, and story 080 (the only story naming f929b5b as its base) contains the string "openzeppelin" nowhere and neither authorises nor presupposes it.
impact: Storage-layout equivalence between the audited/tested build and the mainnet build is no longer guaranteed for four contracts, one of which is live. Any future work that does depend on layout — an upgrade path, a storage-slot read, a `vm.load`-based test, a forked-state comparison — would be reasoning from the wrong layout and would not be told. There is no exploit and no current behavioural change, so this is Low and is a build-hygiene / reproducibility finding, not a vulnerability.
evidence: foundry.toml remappings block (9 canonicalizing entries); `forge build` -> EXIT 0; per-file diffs of Ownable/SafeERC20/EnumerableSet/ERC4626 across the six drifting OZ checkouts; OZ 5.5.0 ReentrancyGuard ERC-7201 migration; version pins in lib/stable-yield-accumulator (5.1.0) and lib/vault (5.4.0); full story-tree enumeration (81 files) returning zero hits for the pin. Antimatter confirmed inert: no `antimatter` string in foundry.toml and no imports under script/, src/ or test/.
recommendation: Pin the top-level OpenZeppelin to a version at or below the lowest pin among the canonicalized submodules (5.1.0 here) so the built layout matches the deployed one, OR bump the submodules' own pins so every consumer genuinely targets 5.6.1 and the mainnet contracts are redeployed from that build. Whichever is chosen, add a `forge inspect <contract> storage-layout` snapshot test for `StableYieldAccumulator` and the three strategies so a future dependency bump that shifts a slot fails loudly. And file the story: this is a cross-cutting dependency change with no acceptance criteria anywhere.

title: Shipped work with no story at all: the OpenZeppelin pin, the 108-file archives sweep and the 246-key package.json purge have no acceptance criteria, and all nine delta commits are untagged
description:
Law 2 grading of the `1d8a3a7..f929b5b` delta. All nine commits carry ZERO `[story-NNN]` tags. The complete story tree was enumerated — `find ~/code/product-owner/stories/phStaging2 -type f -name '*.md'` -> 81 files across every state and sprint folder, highest number 080 — so the following is an established absence, not an unavailability of external documents:
  - OpenZeppelin top-level v5.6.1 pin + 9 canonicalizing remappings: NO STORY EXISTS.
  - `script/archives/**` sweep (108 files moved) + the `skip` directive: NO STORY EXISTS. The only archives mandate anywhere is story 080's two-file `git mv` OUT of archives, which says "Do not touch them; they are mainnet history" and explicitly REJECTS removing the skip.
  - Deletion of 246 package.json keys: NO STORY EXISTS. Story 075 ADDS `promotion-ready:verify`; nothing anywhere authorises removing it.

Two further Law-2 defects: (i) story 080, the only story naming f929b5b as its base commit, is complete-and-reviewed but sits on the UNMERGED branch `sprint/stable-staker-v2` whose merge-base with master is exactly f929b5b — so master carries the code without the story that governs it; (ii) the two story-079 contradictions filed separately above (gating `_seedNudgeStream`, modifying a `package.json` key) were both explicitly forbidden by 079's own text.

This compounds standing ledger entry `Q-01 1c98937375ad` (open), which already records that the story-079 baseline has no acceptance criteria to be graded against.
impact: Three cross-cutting changes — one altering dependency resolution for the entire build, one removing 108 files from compilation, one removing 246 operator entry points — shipped to master with nothing to grade them against and no reviewer checklist that would have caught the concrete defects they introduced (the wagmi silent drop, the dead verify harness, the orphaned promotion-ready runbook, the storage-layout divergence). Each of those is filed separately with its own evidence; this entry is the systemic root. Low as a severity, but it is the finding that explains the others.
evidence: `git -C lib/phoenix-phase-2-staging log --format='%h%x09%s' 1d8a3a7..f929b5b` -> 9 commits, 0 story tags; full story-tree enumeration (81 files, max 080); story 080 text (base commit f929b5b, no 'openzeppelin' string, archives instruction); story 079 text (nudge-stream and package.json prohibitions); `git branch --contains` / merge-base of `sprint/stable-staker-v2` with master -> f929b5b; ledger Q-01 1c98937375ad.
recommendation: Write (or retro-write) stories with acceptance criteria for the three untracked changes before any further work builds on them — at minimum the OZ pin needs a stated compatibility target and the package.json purge needs an explicit list of what was intentionally retired versus swept. Merge `sprint/stable-staker-v2` or revert the story-080 code from master so code and story travel together. Restore `[story-NNN]` tagging on commits; the nine untagged commits are what made this delta ungradeable in the first place.

title: `_seedNudgeStream`'s NatSpec justifies its load-bearing assertion with a claim about `collectNudge` that stopped being true when ledger M-01 was fixed
impact: A future reader — human or agent — reasoning about whether the streamer is safe against taxed tokens will be told by this comment that the in-contract guard does not exist, when it does; conversely, anyone deciding whether the script-level require can be relaxed will over-weight it. Documentation drift only, no behavioural consequence. Low, and reported because the comment explicitly designates itself load-bearing, which is precisely the kind of self-certifying in-source claim that should not be taken on trust.
evidence: DeployMocks.s.sol:2071-2080 vs lib/nft-staking/src/NudgeStreamer.sol `collectNudge` (quoted above), resolved through remappings.txt:86 `nft-staking/=lib/nft-staking/src/` and DeployMocks.s.sol:72.
recommendation: Rewrite the comment to describe the current contract: `collectNudge` measures the received delta and caps it at `amount`, so the script-level `require(received == amount)` is now a stricter local check that the MOCK token is not taxed (which would silently change the seeded rate), not a defence against streamer over-credit. Cross-reference the M-01 fix so the two stay in sync. Propose M-01 (a753907e2a4c) FIXED — propose only, no ledger status changed here.

title: `dev` requires `ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY` but neither sets it nor documents it anywhere the operator will look
description:
`DeployMocks.s.sol:387` reads `vm.envUint("ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY")` with no default and no `envOr` fallback. The `dev` key does not set it, there is no `.envrc` or `.env.example` in the submodule that supplies it, and its only documentation is a line in the project `CLAUDE.md:476` naming the well-known anvil account-0 key `0xac0974bec...ff80`. Without it exported, the whole chain aborts at step 2 with a bare `forge` environment error, AFTER pipeline A has already started a background anvil that then survives as an orphan — which is the stale-chain precondition for the race finding above.

By contrast `LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU` at :398 uses `vm.envOr` with a sensible default, so the pattern for handling this correctly already exists three lines away.
impact: First-run failure for any new developer or CI job, with an unhelpful error and an orphaned anvil left behind. The key itself is the public anvil test key, so there is no secret-handling concern — this is purely an onboarding footgun. Low.
evidence: DeployMocks.s.sol:387 (`vm.envUint`) vs :398 (`vm.envOr`); package.json:16 does not set it; no `.envrc`/`.env.example` in the submodule; CLAUDE.md:476.
recommendation: Use `vm.envOr("ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY", uint256(0xac0974bec39a17e36ba4a6b4d238ff944bacb478cbed5efcae784d7bf4f2ff80))` — it is the standard public anvil account-0 key and the script is chain-31337-only, so defaulting it is safe and removes the failure entirely. If an explicit opt-in is preferred instead, set it in the `dev` key and add a `.env.example`, and add a `require` with a message naming the variable so the failure is self-explaining.

title: `dev` has no terminating success signal: `serve` blocks forever, so the entry point can never exit 0 and cannot be gated in CI
description:
The final step of the `dev` chain is `npm run serve` -> `node server/index.js`, an Express server that blocks indefinitely. `dev` therefore has no exit-0 condition: success is judged by a human reading console output. Verified by running the chain under `timeout --foreground 1750 npm run dev`, which was required precisely because the command has no natural end.

Three consequences compound with findings already filed: (i) `dev` cannot be used as a CI gate, so none of DeployMocks' ~40 in-script assertions ever run automatically; (ii) Ctrl-C kills the foreground server but leaves pipeline A's backgrounded anvil alive, which is the stale-chain precondition for the race finding; (iii) because `/health` returns 200 unconditionally (filed separately), there is no reliable programmatic signal of a good run from outside either.

The orphan was confirmed directly at teardown rather than inferred. After killing `serve`, `npm run dev` returned EXIT 0 while pipeline A's anvil was still alive — `pgrep -af anvil` -> pid 63568 `npm run start:anvil` plus 63594/63595 `anvil --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8545 --chain-id 31337 --block-time 2`, and `eth_chainId` on 8545 still answering `0x7a69`. It had to be killed by PID. So the exact stale-chain precondition for the race finding is produced by the ordinary, successful way this entry point ends.
impact: The local rehearsal of the mainnet cutover — the run that exercises the PhlimboV2->V3 migration, the dispatcher swap and the terminal privilege sweep — is not machine-verifiable. Its assertions only protect anyone who happens to run it by hand and read the output. Local-only, so Low, but it is the reason the other defects in this cluster went undetected across a nine-commit delta.
evidence: package.json:16 (final step `npm run serve`); `timeout --foreground 1750 npm run dev` -> DEV_EXIT=124; server/index.js (Express `app.listen`, no exit path). Teardown: `pgrep -af anvil` after `serve` was killed (pids 63568/63594/63595 alive), `eth_chainId` -> 0x7a69, explicit `kill -9` required.
recommendation: Split the chain: add a `dev:ci` (or `bootstrap:local`) key that runs everything up to and including `generate:ts-anvil`, then exits 0 — that is the part with assertions and the part CI needs — and leave `dev` as `npm run dev:ci && npm run serve` for interactive use. Add a `trap 'kill $ANVIL_PID' EXIT` (or `concurrently --kill-others`) so terminating the foreground also tears down anvil. Then wire `dev:ci` into CI so DeployMocks' assertions actually run on every commit.

title: The deployment progress file the API serves is written during the SIMULATION pass, ~15 minutes before the transactions it certifies are mined, and is never refreshed afterwards
description:
`run()` calls `_writeProgressFile()` at :1564, after `vm.stopBroadcast()` at :1560. `_writeProgressFile` uses `vm.writeJson` (a cheatcode, not a transaction), so it executes during forge's local SIMULATION pass — before a single transaction has been dispatched — and is never re-run after the broadcast completes.

Proved by file mtimes on the full clean run: `DEV_START=2026-09-07T11:28:36`; `server/deployments/progress.31337.json` mtime `2026-09-07 11:28`; `ONCHAIN EXECUTION COMPLETE & SUCCESSFUL` and `broadcast/DeployMocks.s.sol/31337/run-latest.json` at `11:43`. The artifact asserting `"deploymentStatus": "completed"` for 72 contracts predates the 394 transactions that deploy them by roughly fifteen minutes.

Consequence: if the broadcast leg fails, reverts, is interrupted, or (per the race finding) lands on the wrong chain, `progress.31337.json` still reads `completed` with all 72 contracts and their addresses — because it was written from the simulation, where everything always succeeds. `server/index.js` then loads exactly that file and serves it from `/progress`, `/contracts` and the startup banner. I confirmed this end-to-end mid-audit: an earlier run whose broadcast was cut off partway still left a `completed` progress file behind.

DISTINCT FROM ledger L-01 `1e8cc0dc58ba` (open), which records that the status string is hard-coded to "completed". That is about the VALUE written; this is about WHEN it is written. Fixing the hard-coded string alone would not help, because at write time the broadcast genuinely has not started and no honest status is available yet.
impact: The single artifact that everything downstream — the API, the generated TypeScript address bindings, and any human checking whether the stack came up — treats as the record of a deployment is a record of a dry run. It cannot distinguish a successful broadcast from a failed one, an interrupted one, or one applied to a stale chain. Local-only, so Low, but it is the mechanism by which the other failure modes in this cluster stay invisible.
evidence: DeployMocks.s.sol:1560 (`vm.stopBroadcast()`), :1564 (`_writeProgressFile()`), :2620-2646 (`vm.writeJson`); mtime of server/deployments/progress.31337.json (11:28) vs broadcast/DeployMocks.s.sol/31337/run-latest.json (11:43) on the full clean run; `DEV_START=2026-09-07T11:28:36+02:00` in scratchpad/dev-full.log; server/index.js:19-23.
recommendation: Move the progress write out of the forge script and into a post-broadcast step that reads `broadcast/DeployMocks.s.sol/31337/run-latest.json` — the file forge writes only after `ONCHAIN EXECUTION COMPLETE & SUCCESSFUL` — and derives status and per-contract deployment from the actual receipts. A minimal version: add a `node server/build-progress.js 31337` step to `deploy:local` after the forge invocation, and have `_writeProgressFile` stamp `"deploymentStatus": "simulated"` so an unconverted artifact is self-identifying rather than falsely reassuring.
